extraction.name: SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation
extraction.description: SeamlessM4T is a unified system that supports speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages. It was built using 1 million hours of open speech audio data and a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations (SeamlessAlign) totaling 470,000 hours, combined with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data.
extraction.creator: Seamless Communication, Meta AI, INRIA, UC Berkeley
extraction.citeAs: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault, Yu-An Chung, et al. SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation. arXiv:2308.11596, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection involved gathering raw audio and text data at scale from publicly available repositories of crawled web data. This included 4 million hours of raw audio, which was pre-processed (deduplication, resampling, filtering non-speech data). Speech language identification (LID) was performed, and audio was segmented. Parallel data mining was conducted using the Sonar embedding space to align speech segments with text sentences or other speech segments. The final dataset combined this mined data with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some samples from the evaluation data (CVSS) were missing in 8 out of 21 languages. Additionally, some languages were evaluated as zero-shot due to lack of supervised data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, and text datasets drawn from NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Raw audio was deduplicated, resampled to 16KHz, and filtered for non-speech data using an audio event detection model. Audio was segmented using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and over-segmentation. Text was segmented. Speech and text were projected into a joint embedding space (Sonar) for mining parallel pairs. Toxicity filters and length filters were applied to remove noisy or misaligned pairs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio was resampled to 16KHz, filtered for non-speech, and segmented. Text was cleaned and filtered. Special tokens were removed from verbatim transcriptions. Length filtering was applied to remove examples exceeding maximum text length or skewed text-to-audio ratios. Toxicity imbalance filtering was applied. A custom tokenizer was trained to improve coverage of Chinese characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-labeled data was used for S2TT and S2ST tasks. Pseudo-labeling was performed using NLLB-200-3.3B for ASR data. Human evaluations were conducted using the XSTS protocol for translation quality and MOS protocol for naturalness. Toxicity and bias were evaluated using automated metrics (ETOX, ASR-ETOX) and human analysis of detected items.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation involved 3 annotators per item, with additional annotators for disagreements. Median scores were used for robustness. Calibration sets were used to correct annotator bias. Toxicity detection had high false positive rates in Fleurs but high true positive rates in HolisticBias.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (typically), up to 5 in case of disagreement
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLLB-200-3.3B (for pseudo-labeling), ETOX (for toxicity detection), Whisper-Large-v2 (for ASR in evaluation metrics)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The models, inference code, fine-tuning recipes, and metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign are open-sourced and accessible at https://github.com/facebookresearch/seamless_communication. No specific versioning or update schedule is mentioned.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data was mined from publicly available web sources. The authors note that personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated despite data cleaning efforts.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The system aims to augment world-readiness, facilitate multilingual contact, and improve accessibility for individuals with visual impairments or those in regions with script variance. It may also make groups with lower digital literacy more vulnerable to misinformation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model exhibits gender bias, overgeneralizing to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (average preference of ~10%) and showing lack of robustness when varying gender (~3%). Masculine representation is predominant in the analyzed datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model is not intended for production deployment, domain-specific inputs (medical/legal), or long-form translation. It may produce toxic, biased, or false outputs. Performance may vary based on gender, race, accent, or language. Speech translation may carry higher interactional risks in live conversations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Research in speech and text translation, including ASR, S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, and T2TT. Not for certified translations or high-stakes situations involving legal or medical decision-making.
